text:
carlos_sales: Quick sync — prospect GlobalBank needs EU-only data residency for a POC and production. They want: full subprocessors list, confirmation control+data plane can stay in EU, BYOK, and the pricing delta for Dedicated vs Hosted. Anyone able to confirm feasibility + rough numbers? CC @nina_deals

hana_presales: We can support EU-only for the POC via tenant pinning to EU regions. Options are: Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Private (VPC/control-plane in EU). Hosted default control plane is in US unless we enable EU control plane for the customer (enterprise setup). BYOK is supported on Dedicated and Private. Subprocessors list: https://redwood.com/docs/subprocessors (link to canonical CSV). :eyes:

leo_security: Quick security note: subprocessors CSV is available to legal. Logs/telemetry retention can be disabled per-tenant. Data plane (inference) stays in-region when tenant-pinned; prefix/KV cache is in-region for pinned tenants. If you need strict control-plane in EU (no metadata leaving EU) advise Private. For production-grade EU-only residency we'll require DPA + SCC/UK Addendum or equivalent. :lock:

nina_deals: Pricing note for planning: for the POC (6 weeks) with reserved Dedicated EU capacity, expect a delta of roughly $8k–$12k/month above base hosted costs for the throughput you described. Private deployment has higher fixed onboarding + infra fees — I can run numbers if you give qps/seq len.

carlos_sales: Targets: steady 15 qps, burst to 45 qps, avg sequence length ~256 tokens. BYOK required (customer-managed KMS). Also — customer strict requirement: no cross-border fallback to non-EU without explicit approval. Can we enforce that?

hana_presales: Yes — routing policy can be set to strict geo-pin with fallback disabled. Behaviour options: queue requests, return 429 when capacity exceeded, or hold for ops intervention. We'll need an ops ticket to lock tenant-level fallback to false. Example config we typically use (ops/UI sets this):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  geo_pin: eu-west-1
  allow_fallback: false
  degrade_behavior: queue
  kms: customer_byo_kms
```
I'll open the ticket and include the POC dates.

leo_security: Checklist for legal/security: subprocessors CSV, signed DPA, SOC2 report, key envelope flow docs for BYOK, IP allowlist CIDRs, and confirmation telemetry disabled if requested. Also confirm analytics/observability vendor participation — can be turned off for this tenant. I'll prepare the questionnaire items. :paperclip:

ops_bot: New internal request created: POC-3821 — Presales -> Dedicated EU tenant pinning. Owner: @marie_ops. Initial capacity reservation ETA: 3 business days.

nina_deals: I'll draft a ballpark quote and attach our standard DPA and the subprocessors CSV. @carlos_sales please confirm PoC start date so I can lock pricing.

carlos_sales: Target PoC start 2025-04-15. And one more Q from the customer: do your subprocessors include any US-based analytics vendor that might touch control-plane metadata? Need explicit yes/no per vendor.

hana_presales: Our list includes: cloud infra (EU-provider-1), observability relay (redwood-obsv-eu), model mirror caches (read-only EU mirrors). We do have an analytics partner used on the control plane by default (US-based) but it can be disabled for enterprise tenants / turned off during the POC. I'll get infra/legal to produce a per-vendor EU-only impact statement.

leo_security: If analytics is to be disabled, we will disable telemetry ingestion for the tenant and provide attestation. Need customer's legal contact to sign off. :white_check_mark:

carlos_sales: Great — next steps: @nina_deals create quote + DPA, @hana_presales confirm exact deployment options and open ops ticket to enforce allow_fallback=false, @leo_security prepare the security questionnaire + attestation text. I'll tee up the customer call this week. TY! :thumbsup:
